newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's CIB seeking $100 mln syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's CIB seeking $100 mln syndicated loan.

text.p: Commercial International Bank (CIB) of Egypt said on Wednesday it was seeking a $100 million three-year syndicated loan and had mandated Chase Investment Bank Ltd and Union Bank of Switzerland to arrange it.

It will be the first syndicated loan by an Egyptian borrower for 15 years and the bank will use the loan for "general funding purposes", CIB managing director Adel El-Labban said in a written statement.

"Syndication will focus on U.S., European, Middle Eastern and Asian banks to benefit from funds inflows attracted by Egypt's investment-grade rating (BBB- by Standard and Poor's) and CIB's excellent relationship with the international banking community," Labban added.
ING Barings and Commerzbank will act as joint lead arrangers and invitations are going out to form the co-arrangers group, he said.
CIB, Egypt's largest private-sector bank and the only one with shares traded internationally, said it was also planning to issue a domestic Egyptian pound floating-rate note.

"Opportunities to issue Eurodebt securities in the second half of the year are also under consideration subject to favourable market conditions," the statement added. "CIB is aiming to diversify and lengthen its sources of funding at competitive costs to support projected asset growth."
In January CIB shareholders gave the board clearance to raise up to 900 million pounds ($265 million) by issuing pound or foreign currency bonds or floating-rate notes over two years.
The proposal put to shareholders was for Egyptian pound instruments up to a value of 500 million pounds and foreign currency instruments up to the equivalent of 400 million pounds.
Bank executives were not available to say how exactly the syndicated loan would affect its other borrowing plans.
Other Cairo-based banks have resorted mainly to Egyptian-pound bonds as sources of long-term funding. But the interest on these is much higher than on dollar borrowings.
